transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration approx: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ava Brooks (CSM), Luis Ramirez (Carmine Head of MLOps), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), Sophie Le (CTO)

Auto-summary:
Carmine is planning a renewal with a capacity uplift and wants to add EU region staging (eu-west-2). Main asks: predictable latency under 150ms p50, data residency for EU traffic, SOC2 + SSO integration, and a procurement timeline that aligns with Q3 budget. Redwood outlined dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, proposed a staged activation (hosted eu then Dedicated private VPC pilot), and agreed to run benchmarks and share updated pricing.

Topics covered:
- Current usage profile and burst characteristics
- Region activation sequence and failover
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
- Pricing options: reserved capacity, burst, pay-as-you-go
- Technical validation: latency targets, KV cache behavior, quantization implications

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we'll keep to 45 minutes. Quick roll call, then jump into renewal numbers and the eu region ask.
[00:00:12] Sophie: hi, sorry, running a touch late but I'm here; thanks.
[00:00:20] Luis: good afternoon all.
[00:00:30] Jordan: great. So Carmine, last quarter usage grew ~2.3x across inference - is that still the right ballpark?
[00:00:45] Priya: yes, on average, month over month we're seeing 12-15% and spikes are more like 3x for certain campaigns. The EU traffic is about 28% of total and latency sensitive so we want eu-west-2 activated as primary for EU users.
[00:01:05] Maya (SE): ok, when you say latency sensitive, are we talking p50 or p95 targets?
[00:01:12] Priya: p50 under 150ms, p95 under 350ms ideally.
[00:01:20] Jordan: noted. For p50 150ms that's generally achievable on Hosted in eu-west-2 for the base model, but it depends on batching and context size.
[00:01:35] Luis: our typical requests are 800–1,200 tokens, KV cache is used per session, so cold-starts matter. We also have a few long-context flows 6k-8k tokens.
[00:01:50] Maya: ok; cold-start is the hard one. We can recommend prefix caching and 2-layer routing so EU traffic hits eu cluster first, and we can pre-warm. For big contexts (6–8k) we may suggest a quantized variant for cost savings, but we'll validate quality.
[00:02:10] Sophie: question on residency: we need logs and raw user data not to leave EU. Can Redwood provide EU data residency and KMS key control?
[00:02:25] Jordan: yes — for Dedicated + Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs in-region. Hosted EU has logical separation and retention controls but not customer-managed HSM today. If residency is a hard req, we should scope a Private VPC pilot.
[00:02:48] Luis: ok, procurement prefers hosted first to reduce ops overhead, but compliance may force Private later. So staged approach make sense.
[00:02:58] Maya: then our suggested flow: 1) activate hosted eu-west-2 region for immediate latency improvement, 2) run a 2-week perf soak with synthetic and real traffic, 3) if residency or encryption needs surface, kick off private VPC pilot with dedicated nodes. That pilot typically takes 4–6 weeks setup.
[00:03:25] Priya: can you remind me on the lead time for Dedicated GPU pool provisioning?
[00:03:33] Jordan: dedicated provisioning for a standard reserve is ~3–4 weeks, private VPC can be 4–8 depending on networking approvals and KMS integration.
[00:03:45] [Speaker 1]: and costs — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
[00:03:50] Maya: high level: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token/embedding and is best for elasticity. Dedicated is a monthly reserved commitment with lower unit cost at scale and stronger isolation. For Carmine's numbers we sketched an uplift SKU that reduces per-token by ~25% at 3T tokens/mo committed. I'll share the spreadsheet.
[00:04:10] Priya: sounds good. Luis: any blockers from security side?
[00:04:16] Luis: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 are checkboxes, also SSO SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We need audit log granularity: per-token traces and per-request headers for compliance.
[00:04:30] Ava (CSM): we can share the SOC2 report and our compliance pack; we've done SAML and SCIM integrations with Okta for other customers.
[00:04:40] Sophie: great, please send the compliance pack.
[00:04:45] [00:05:00] Maya: technical question — for the long context flows, are you using KV cache cross-session or per-user?
[00:05:10] Priya: per-user session, we persist KV for up to 30 minutes. Some flows stitch multiple requests in a single long convo.
[00:05:21] Maya: ok that helps. One note: large KV caches increase memory pressure and may affect throughput; our runtime has dynamic KV eviction and we can tune cache TTLs per route. There's also continuous batching heuristics — if you have many concurrent short requests, batching improves throughput but adds latency.
[00:05:43] Luis: the tradeoff is real — some product flows need <200ms, others can tolerate 500–700ms. We want default low-latency for search/autocomplete and relaxed for async summarization.
[00:05:58] Jordan: that's where routing policies help: tag requests by route and apply different batching windows and quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize will suggest per-route configs but you'll still be able to override.
[00:06:15] Sophie: what's Redwood Optimize? I think we missed the product naming earlier in the deck.
[00:06:20] Jordan: sorry, the name is Redwood Optimize — cost/perf toolkit we ship — it gives batching, quantization recs and cache settings tied to traffic patterns.
[00:06:28] Priya: any concerns about model fidelity if we quantize for the 6–8k flows?
[00:06:35] Maya: we typically run A/B evals — quantized models give small degradations but for many summarization or classification tasks it's acceptable. We'll run evals with your dev set.
[00:06:48] [00:07:00] Luis: timeline: if we sign a renewal now, can we get EU region activated within 2 weeks on hosted?
[00:07:07] Jordan: yes — hosted region activation is fast, often 3–10 business days to get routing and quotas in place. We'll need your traffic profile and SSO certs to configure egress and auth.
[00:07:20] Sophie: procurement note — our legal wants a term of 12 months with an option to extend; budget approval by early July.
[00:07:30] Jordan: ok; we can propose a 12-month commitment with a mid-term addendum for Private if needed, and a checkpoint in 90 days.
[00:07:40] Priya: we also want to test failover — if eu is down, can traffic route to us-east-1 without leaking EU data? That's critical.
[00:07:50] Maya: yes, you can configure geo-failover policies; to prevent data leaving EU you can set strict routing plus a fallback to a compliant fallback endpoint (e.g., a Private cluster in EU). We'll document options: soft-failover (some data may cross) vs hard-failover (block requests).
[00:08:12] [00:08:30] Luis: what about auditing and per-route tracing — do you store token-level traces by default?
[00:08:38] Jordan: by default we collect request/response metadata and cost metrics. Token-level traces are available in Dedicated/Private with extended retention; Hosted has masked transcripts and configurable retention to meet privacy needs.
[00:08:55] Sophie: we need to see examples of audit logs format.
[00:08:58] Ava: I'll attach the log schema + sample in the follow-up.
[00:09:05] [00:09:30] Maya: technical point — for your benchmarks, what client libraries are you using? Are you already on the new streaming SDK?
[00:09:38] Priya: we're using an internal wrapper over REST, not yet on streaming. We can try streaming for the throughput tests.
[00:09:45] Maya: cool, streaming helps tail latency when you have large tokens; we'll include a streaming test.
[00:09:55] [00:10:30] Jordan: quick pricing note — for the proposed uplift we're recommending a 12-month reserve for EU with a 3T tokens/month commitment and burst buffer; the upsell delta vs current is roughly +30% month-on-month but effective unit cost drops. I'll send the detailed SKU math.
[00:10:48] Luis: can you also include a break-even analysis vs AltoAI — they're pitching aggressive price but no private option.
[00:10:58] Jordan: yes, we'll include competitor delta and risk analysis — uptime SLA, data residency, and support coverage.
[00:11:10] [00:11:30] Sophie: procurement will want an exit clause if private pilot doesn't pass.
[00:11:36] Jordan: typical addendum we include is a 30-day remediation + rollback clause for private pilots; we'll propose language for legal.
[00:11:45] [00:12:00] Priya: on the perf tests — we can do a mixture of synthetic and replayed traffic. We have a replay harness but need to sanitize PII.
[00:12:10] Maya: understood. For replay we'll provide guidance and a small tooling script to scrub PII.
[00:12:20] Luis: also want to validate model version pinning — we need consistent outputs across rollouts.
[00:12:28] Maya: you can pin model versions per route and we support canary rollouts with automatic fallback to last good version. We'll show that in the pilot.
[00:12:40] [00:13:00] Sophie: any network requirements for VPC?
[00:13:06] Jordan: we'll need your peering/XPN details and firewall rules; Private VPC requires static IPs and cross account peering. We'll provide a checklist.
[00:13:20] Priya: ok, Priya: I'll pull that together.
[00:13:25] [00:14:00] Jordan: next up — benchmarks. Maya, can you outline proposed tests now?
[00:14:06] Maya: sure. Plan: 1) small-context latency test (256 tokens) to capture p50/p95, 2) long-context throughput test (6–8k) with quant + non-quant runs, 3) burst soak to simulate 3x spikes for 1 hour. We'll run these in hosted eu-west-2, and optionally in Dedicated snapshot if you want to compare ded vs hosted.
[00:14:34] Luis: we want the dedicated comparison; procurement will ask.
[00:14:38] Jordan: noted. We'll schedule two runs — hosted baseline and dedicated baseline. Dedicated run will require provisioning time.
[00:14:48] [00:15:30] Maya: for the dedicated baseline we can use a temporary dev cluster or a short commit — we'll scope costs in the pricing sheet.
[00:15:40] Priya: what's the expected quality delta for quantized models?
[00:15:46] Maya: usually small for summarization tasks — 1–3% metric drop on our evals. We'll run your evals.
[00:15:58] [00:16:30] Sophie: can Redwood support our SAML JIT provisioning and SCIM for user accounts?
[00:16:36] Jordan: yes, SAML + SCIM supported. We'll need metadata and the cert.
[00:16:44] Priya: we'll send SSO cert and Okta details this week.
[00:16:50] [00:17:30] Luis: are there any hard limits we should know about for sequence length?
[00:17:36] Maya: runtime supports up to 32k in some variants but you'll pay more for long contexts; also KV caching and memory will be the gating factor. We'll map your expected 8k flows to a recommended model and a quant profile.
[00:17:55] [00:18:30] Jordan: quick recap so far: staged approach (hosted eu activation -> perf tests -> optional private VPC pilot), Redwood to run hosted + dedicated benchmarks, Redwood to send pricing and compliance pack.
[00:18:45] Sophie: yes that's right.
[00:19:00] Priya: question on pricing — will the 3T tokens/mo commitment be flexible? We may need to scale after 60 days.
[00:19:10] Jordan: contracts can include step-ups at predefined checkpoints; we typically do a 90-day review and allow amendments.
[00:19:20] Luis: are there penalties for overage?
[00:19:25] Jordan: overage is billed at tiered pay-as-you-go rates; for committed customers we also offer temporary burst buffers.
[00:19:35] [00:20:00] Maya: one more technical nuance — when we say "KV cache", transcripts sometimes say K V cash in logs so just call it KV cache to avoid confusion.
[00:20:10] Priya: noted.
[00:20:30] [00:21:00] Jordan: okay next steps, I'll outline the timeline and share the pricing deck after this call. Maya will own benchmark runs. Ava will send compliance artifacts. Priya will provide traffic and SSO details.
[00:21:20] Sophie: procurement target early July for sign-off. If we can show hosted eu p50 <150ms and Dedicated reduces unit cost as promised, we can align budget.
[00:21:35] Luis: one last ask — include a simple diagram in the follow-up that shows routing and where data lives for hosted vs private.
[00:21:45] Jordan: will do.
[00:22:00] [00:22:30] Maya: I'll book engineering benchmark timeslots — propose Tuesday/Thursday next week.
[00:22:40] Priya: Tuesday morning works for us.
[00:22:48] [00:23:30] Jordan: any final questions?
[00:23:35] Sophie: none from me. Thanks all.
[00:23:45] Luis: thanks team.
[00:24:00] Jordan: we'll follow up with an email capturing action items.
